title: Vanishing of the gate count through layer zero
statement: Let $F$ be a layered feedforward circuit over the Boolean alphabet $\{0,1\}$, whose input layer carries $n$ nodes and each of whose layers has a finite node set. Then the number of non-input gates lying in the first $0$ layers is zero, since the input layer contributes no gates.
hypotheses_covered: feedforward circuit $F$ over the Boolean alphabet $\{0,1\}$ with an $n$-element input layer
each layer of $F$ has a finite node set
$0$ is at most the depth of $F$
replaced: $\mathrm{gateCountBefore}\,F\,0 = 0$: the input layer contributes no gates.
